title: Senior Clinical Trials Statistician
description: About the Role An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated Statistician to join the Critical Care & Perioperative Medicine Research Group. The Group sits within the William Harvey Research Institute at Queen Mary University of London under the leadership of Professor Rupert Pearse. About You The post holder will provide statistical support for research studies including multi-centre clinical trials, assist in design of new studies and ensure that data is analysed accurately to maximise the quality of publishable results from research studies that they work on. They will be responsible for developing statistical analysis plans, performing data cleaning, conducting statistical analysis, and preparing scientific reports. They will also support the development of large prospective clinical trials and analyse clinical datasets in collaboration with national and international groups focused on improving survival after major surgery. We are looking for a talented individual with a postgraduate qualification, including a major statistical component, and an interest in evaluating novel treatments or interventions of pharmaceuticals, surgery, medical devices or complex interventions. You will have applied experience in clinical trial statistics and/or medical statistics including some project and people management. You should be a good communicator, team-player and be flexible, co-operative, self-motivated and hardworking with a willingness to learn new skills. About the School/Department/Institute/Project Professor Pearse and his team lead a wide variety of research projects that have a major impact both nationally and globally. If you are interested in research on topics such as improving outcomes following major surgery, critical illness, polytrauma and acute kidney injury then this is the team for you. The group includes Prof Gareth Ackland, Dr John Prowle, Prof Zudin Puthucheary, Clinical Lecturers, Research Fellows and PhD students. This post allows you to join a world leading research programme that prioritises excellence in all areas. About Queen Mary At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable. Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers. We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form. Benefits We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities. Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly. £54,617 to £60,901 per annum

title: Clinical Trial Delivery Manager - UOD2331
description: We are seeking an exceptional Clinical Trial Delivery Manager to join the Health Informatics Centre at the University of Dundee. You will play a key role in supporting and advancing clinical trial recruitment through data -enabled research and informatics services with the Health Informatics Centre (HIC) at the University of Dundee. This is a highly collaborative role which is both externally and internally focused , with a strong emphasis on HIC’s clinical trial capability, stakeholder engagement and data - enabled research delivery . A core focus of the role is to bridge the gap between clinical trial units, NHS partners and delivery teams by translating complex clinical trial and technical requirements into clear, actionable deliverables. As HIC’s Clinical Trial Delivery Manager , you will play an important role in facilitating coordination for clinical trial informatics activities, bringing together partners, platforms and HIC delivery teams to ensure a unified approach. You will manage the delivery of complex, high -impact projects, while strengthening collaboration between NHS organisations, academia, clinical trial units and other stakeholders. The role requires a proactive and adaptable individual who can bring together diverse stakeholder groups , translating complex technical concepts into clear , actionable requirements and delivery plans. Key responsibilities You will be responsible for: Lead ing the delivery of clinical trial informatics projects , coordinating technical solutions that support efficient clinical trial recruitment and delivery. Building and manag ing relationships with NHS, academic and research partners, acting as the key interface between stakeholders and HIC delivery teams. Driving the development of innovative informatics services, identifying opportunities to enhance clinical trial recruitment, data access and digital capabilities. Support ing the growth of HIC's clinical trials portfolio by contributing to strategic initiatives, business development and funding applications. Ensuring high standards of governance and delivery, managing risks and ensuring compliance with information governance, data protection and quality requirements. Collaborat ing across multidisciplinary teams to plan priorities, share knowledge, drive innovation and continuously improve clinical trial informatics services. Who we're looking for essential Educated to degree level or equivalent professional experience. Broad knowledge of IT project management, software development and delivery, service management a nd technical infrastructure. Experience managing complex informatics or clinical research projects. Experience translating business or clinical requirements into technical delivery outputs. Track record of effectively leading and managing change in a complex environment. Experience working within the health sector, ideally involving the use of health data for research or service delivery. Strong stakeholder engagement skills across NHS, academia and industry. Proven ability to work across multiple organisations and influence decision -makers. Excellent verbal and written communication skills to both technical staff and senior management. A team player with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and deliver outputs within agreed timeframes. String problem solving skills with the ability to develop innovate solutions and continuously improve existing processes. Ability to discuss and debate constructively

title: Research Associate in Molecular Virology
description: Location : South Kensington campus About the role : We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral research associate with molecular virology skills to join our team ( www.imperial.ac.uk/barclay-lab ). Our mission is to define how viruses cross species barriers and evolve to infect humans. We are using influenza viruses as models to understand the crucial steps for pandemicity. In this job you will focus on the early events inside the cell that underpin the virus’ ability to replicate in their new host. What you would be doing : You will be validating the roles of a series of novel host factors we have discovered to be associated with the influenza A virus polymerase as it carries out different functions inside the host cell nucleus. You will do this through a combination of bioinformatics and molecular virology techniques. This will involve knocking down expression of the factors and assessing virus replication, looking for in situ colocalization of the factors with viral polymerase, and by comparing the interaction of the factors with viral ribonucleoproteins assembled from positive or negative sense viral RNA. What we are looking for : We are looking for a team member who has previously worked with viruses in mammalian cell systems. It will be great for our team if you can bring in more experience in genetically manipulating cells with CRISPR, generating and/or working with primary cell systems, and/or handling large data sets. We are keen to bring on board someone with experience in using AlphaFold and other bioinformatics packages to apply to our sets of host factors. What we can offer you : Be part of a diverse team who work together on one of today’s big challenges and support each other to advance our knowledge and careers. The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects. Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing . Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant . Time (35 h/w) post and a fixed-term contract for 24 months. Expected start date January 1 st 2027. The Barclay lab team consists of 6 postdoctoral associates, three technicians and a lab manager. Everyone in the group works on respiratory viruses with pandemic potential, and our work spans from discovery of host factors that affect the outcome of infection, through using complex models of airway to recapitulate the challenging environments these viruses must negotiate, to designing new vaccines and testing mitigations to block infection and transmission. For further details please contact: Wendy Barclay w.barclay@imperial.ac.uk About Imperial Welcome to Imperial, a global top ten university where scientific imagination leads to world-changing impact.

title: Research Associate in Host Immunity
description: Location : Hammersmith Campus (and occasionally other Imperial College London sites) About the role : Do you want to lead high-dimensional immunology research to tackle one of the world's important bacterial pathogens? Staphylococcus aureus is a leading cause of life-threatening infection worldwide, yet current prevention and treatment strategies remain limited by a lack of defined human correlates of protection. As a Post-Doctoral Research Associate within Dr Dinesh Aggarwal’s group, you will play a role in a controlled human infection study designed to address this need. Working at the forefront of translational infection biology, you will lead the design, validation, and execution of advanced cellular and humoral immunology techniques. Your work will map local and systemic immune responses during this human challenge study; by analysing complex immunological datasets, you will help define correlates of protection to support vaccine and therapeutic development in the fight against Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), a mission of the Fleming Initiative. What you would be doing : You will drive independent research within a multi-disciplinary team of clinicians, research nurses, microbiologists, and industry partners. Leading experimental pipelines including developing and validating advanced methods to evaluate host cellular and humoral immune responses following natural clinical infection and controlled human infection with S. aureus . Leading the bioinformatics integration and multivariate analysis of high-dimensional immunological data, ensuring reproducibility and driving technical innovation. Writing high-quality manuscripts for publication in leading peer-reviewed journals, presenting findings at national and international conferences, and preparing reports for grant sponsors. Providing day-to-day scientific supervision, training, and mentorship to PhD students, research technicians, and clinical fellows, while contributing to the safe operation of the laboratory. What we are looking for : A PhD (or equivalent) in Immunology, Infection Biology, Immuno-pathology, or a closely related discipline (or imminent award of one). *Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. Substantial postdoctoral or doctoral research experience in an academic or industrial immunology laboratory, supported by first-author publications in peer-reviewed journals and conference presentations. Extensive hands-on experience designing, running, and analysing high-parameter flow cytometry panels, developing and validating functional immunoassays with deep knowledge of human immunology and host-pathogen interactions. Strong working knowledge of biostatistics, multivariate analysis, and high-dimensional datasets. The ability to independently plan, prioritise, and troubleshoot complex research over 3- to 6-month horizon, and the ability and willingness to mentor and supervise PhD students and junior staff. Excellent scientific writing and verbal communication skills to collaborate effectively across a multidisciplinary team. What we can offer you : The chance to contribute to the Fleming Initiative, a transformative partnership tackling AMR through people-centred science. Work within Dr. Dinesh Aggarwal’s group, collaborating with the wider teams of Prof. Chris Chiu, Prof. Shiranee Sriskandan and Dr. Malick Gibani, and external academic and industry partners. The opportunity to drive impactful research in a world-leading research environment, with access to Imperial’s dedicated career support for researchers. A Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days off a year and generous pension schemes). A diverse, inclusive and collaborative culture with staff networks and personal and professional wellbeing support. Further information This is a full-time post and a fixed term for 12 months in the first instance. For more details, please contact: Dr. Dinesh Aggarwal ( d.aggarwal@imperial.ac.uk ).

title: Research Associate
description: Vacancy terms: Full time fixed term contract until 31 December 2033 About the role We are seeking a Post-Doctoral Research Associate (PDRA) to play a key role in the Wellcome-funded project, “ASCEND-HD: Advancing Support and Care for Emotional Needs and Distress in Huntington’s Disease”. Working within the School of Psychology and Vision Sciences, you will contribute to improving understanding of mental wellbeing difficulties in Huntington’s disease, supporting the development of resources for the Huntington’s community and collaborating with academics, healthcare professionals and third-sector organisations. You will undertake qualitative and quantitative research, lead data collection and analysis activities, contribute to patient and public involvement work, and support the dissemination of findings through publications, presentations and wider knowledge exchange activities. Working closely with the project team under the supervision of the project lead, you will take ownership of key project components, contribute to ethics applications and research outputs, and help ensure the successful delivery of a research programme valued at £2 million. The role offers opportunities to contribute to doctoral student supervision, teaching activities and professional development while engaging with national and international collaborators. As part of our research community, you will be expected to attend regular meetings and be present on campus for the majority of the time, though some working from home is possible. About you You will hold, or be close to completing, a PhD or DClinPsy in a relevant psychological or healthcare discipline and you will have significant experience of research involving people affected by neurological conditions. You will have experience of leading substantial qualitative research projects, applying research methods and techniques to produce high-quality outputs, and obtaining informed consent within research studies. Experience of qualitative and quantitative research methods in healthcare or psychological settings and an understanding of Good Clinical Practice will be advantageous. You will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to conduct sensitive one-to-one interviews involving potentially challenging or distressing topics. Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills are essential, alongside a commitment to delivering high-quality research and engaging effectively with participants, collaborators and wider stakeholders. £39,906 to £46,049 per annum: Grade 7

title: Research Associate in Cognitive Neuroscience & AI (Fixed Term)
description: Department/Location: Cambridge Institute for Technology and Humanity, Central Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, UK We are seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to join an exciting programme of research investigating the cognitive and neural mechanisms that underpin language generation. This project combines intracranial electrophysiology (iEEG) with cutting-edge computational modelling using Large Language Models (LLMs) to explore how people produce language in natural, real-world conversations. Working closely with Dr Ariel Goldstein, the successful candidate will contribute to pioneering research at the intersection of cognitive neuroscience, psychology and artificial intelligence. The Research Associate will play a key role in advancing our understanding of how the brain generates and communicates meaningful language. They will design and conduct experiments, analyse neural and behavioural datasets, and develop computational models of language production using LLMs. The postholder will help translate empirical findings into testable theories of language generation, contributing to an ambitious research agenda that integrates experimental and computational approaches to human cognition. As part of the role, the successful candidate will contribute to the dissemination of research through high-quality publications, conference presentations, and engagement with the wider scientific community. They will also support the preparation of reports and funding applications, while helping to foster a collaborative and intellectually stimulating research environment. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious researcher to contribute to internationally significant work addressing fundamental question about language, cognition and the human brain. Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 24 months in the first instance. Please ensure that you upload your 1) Curriculum Vitae (CV), 2) a research publication list, and 3) a covering letter outlining how you match the criteria for the post and why you are applying in the Upload section of the online application. If you upload any additional documents which have not been requested, we will not be able to consider these as part of your application. Please be advised that we will be requesting references in advance of interviews, for longlisted candidates. Please inform your referees that reference letters may be requested shortly after the closing date. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. If you have any questions about this vacancy, please contact Dr Ariel Goldstein ( ag2542@cam.ac.uk ), for questions on the application process, please contact the School's HR Team at: sahhr@admin.cam.ac.uk The closing date for applications is midnight (BST) on Wednesday 9 September 2026. Interviews will be held in the week commencing 21 September 2026, subject to change. Please quote reference GO50857 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK. £37,694 to £46,049 per annum

title: Research Associate in Islamic Art (Fixed Term)
description: The HRH Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Centre of Islamic Studies (CIS) at the University of Cambridge is seeking to appoint a Postdoctoral Research and Outreach Associate in Islamic art and architecture and/or material culture. The post is a three-year, fixed-term position which will commence in September 2027. It is full-time and based in the Centre of Islamic Studies, which is located in the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies. CIS research and outreach posts are distinctive in that postholders are expected to 1) pursue a research project in an area of Islamic art, architecture and/or material culture and 2) design and run a set of outreach activities that reach beyond the academic community. What form the latter will take will depend on the specialism of the appointee but collaboration with the Fitzwilliam Museum, other Cambridge museums, the University Library and local schools is welcomed, as well as proposals for other forms of outreach. CIS is one of a network of HRH Alwaleed Bin Talal centres and research and outreach associates are strongly encouraged to collaborate with colleagues at our UK partner institution, the Alwaleed Centre at the University of Edinburgh and with other Alwaleed centres at Harvard, Georgetown, the American University of Beirut and the American University of Cairo as appropriate. Research and outreach associates are expected to apply for additional external funding for the activities they design, when possible. The postholder may also contribute to the teaching of Islamic art, architecture and material culture within the Department of Middle Eastern Studies, with which CIS has close links, or elsewhere in the University. Candidates will need to demonstrate an upward research trajectory and an ability to develop and carry out research projects of a high academic standard. They will also need to show an interest in and understanding of the remit of the Centre of Islamic Studies and a commitment to outreach beyond academia. Attendance at and participation in CIS weekly seminars and events during term-time, and annual conferences or symposia, is expected. The role requires an ability to work independently but also as part of a team, and native or near native fluency in spoken and written English. The successful candidate will be expected to have been awarded their PhD by the date their employment commences. CIS Research and Outreach posts are intended primarily for early-career researchers. Applications are therefore invited from researchers who have submitted their doctoral thesis for viva voce examination no more than four years prior to the application closing date. Those wishing to make a case for a career break due to maternity leave, family commitments, illness, or other exceptional circumstances should provide relevant details. Please note that time spent working outside academia does not qualify as a career break. The closing date for applications is 15 October 2026. Academic references will be requested for shortlisted candidates in advance of the interviews, which will likely take place towards the end of November. They may take place in-person or online, depending on the applicant's and interviewers’ availability. Any offer of employment will be conditional on the offer-holder having or gaining the right to work in the UK and receipt of a satisfactory workplace reference if relevant.

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Degradable Electronic Polymers
description: Location: Department of Chemistry - Chemistry Research Laboratory, 12 Mansfield Road, Oxford, OX1 3TA Interested in all things polymer? Chromic, Electronic, Degradable? Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Associate to help develop polymers that are electronically functional, degradable, and that shift colour as they break down, so a device can report its own remaining lifetime before it stops working. This post sits at the point where conjugated polymers meet classic cleavable polyester and carbonate chemistry. It is associated with the recently funded EPSRC New Investigator Award "Colour-Changing Electroactive Polymers: Degradation-Responsive Materials for Self-Reporting Electronics". Based in the Department of Chemistry under the supervision of Dr Georgina Gregory, this post is fixed-term for up to 2.5 years. This is a new programme and you would be leading its experimental work in a small, well-equipped group, with room to shape the chemistry and the freedom to follow what the results suggest. Find out more about the Gregory Group at: https://www.chem.ox.ac.uk/people/georgina-gregory About you Applicants must hold a PhD in polymer chemistry, materials chemistry or a closely related field, (or be close to submission), prior to taking up the appointment, with a publication record appropriate to your career stage. Experience of conjugated polymer synthesis or ring-opening polymerisation, conductivity measurements, spectroelectrochemistry, or thin film processing and device fabrication would all be an advantage. The project spans synthesis, degradation and electronic and optical characterisation, and nobody arrives with all of it. You will enjoy learning, and take satisfaction in taking a polymer from synthetic design through to working material. You will be able to work independently, and to work supportively and enthusiastically with others, communicating what you find in writing and in person. There will be the opportunity to supervise an undergraduate project student, and to take an interest and a share of responsibility in the equipment the group depends on. The post is full-time, applications from those wishing to work part-time will be considered, and will be based in the Chemistry Research Laboratory, 12 Mansfield Road, Oxford, OX1 3TA. Applicants must hold a PhD in polymer chemistry, materials chemistry or a closely related field (or close to completion), prior to taking up the appointment. Essential experience includes: Polymer synthesis Standard polymer characterisation techniques Conductivity measurements of polymers You will be expected to manage your own research activities under guidance, contribute to experimental work, analyse and present scientific data, and work collaboratively with colleagues in partner institutions, and research groups, both within the department and externally. The closing date for applications is 12.00 midday on 16 September 2026 , UK time. Interviews will be held as soon as possible thereafter. Please upload a CV and Supporting Statement as part of your online application (via the ' Apply ' button above). Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post, using clear examples drawn from skills and experience. Please note that certificates, references and research papers should not be provided at this stage. £39,424 to £47,779 per annum (inclusive of Oxford University Weighting). Grade 7

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: Full Time: 35 hours per week Fixed term: for 36 months Where discovery never stops. Be part of something bigger. A unique employer in a vibrant city The University isn’t just any employer. We are part of a local community and a contributor to global thinking, progress and research. In Edinburgh, you are in one of the world’s most attractive cities with active arts and social sectors, while working in a University that has made significant contributions to society, medicine, physics and teaching for over four centuries. Our people have helped create the modern world and are working on more ground-breaking technologies and practices. Make a meaningful impact Here, you can continue to make a difference in everything around you. Take on new challenges, grow your career, be recognised for your contributions, and benefit from our commitment to your wellbeing. Be part of something bigger — where your work has real impact and your development matters. There are so many reasons to take your next step with us. The University of Edinburgh is a world-class organisation. We look for the best in the field across all disciplines and provide a working environment where academics can develop their careers and passion for their chosen subject area. We offer the full range of academic roles and have a genuine focus on our students’ performance and wellbeing. The Opportunity: We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher to join the team led by Dr Alice Green in the School of Chemistry. The post holder will work on a new project led by Dr Green to build an advanced time-resolved Coulomb explosion imaging apparatus in the group’s laboratory. This instrument will be used to image, with high fidelity, ultrafast molecular motion that occurs during photochemical reactions of isolated gas-phase molecules. These exciting experimental capabilities will be used to advance our understanding of fundamental photochemical reactivity. The candidate must have completed a PhD degree in Chemistry, Physics, or a related discipline. Experience with ultrafast spectroscopy and charged-particle detection/imaging is essential. This role will involve significant instrument design and practical work. Experience in instrument design and construction, particularly of high-vacuum apparatuses, is therefore highly beneficial. People have always been at the heart of our work. Our people are at the centre of the University community and everything we do. We value colleagues with drive, determination and a passion for what they do. We are a place where everyone is welcome and offer a range of policies and benefits designed to support you in building the right meaningful flexibility that works for you. A career with us has a range of other benefits that can be tailored to your lifestyle: Professional development and subject matter expertise Opportunities to develop new skills and broaden your experience Responsibility and autonomy Apply Before : 02/10/2026, 23:59 £41,064 to £48,822 per annum

title: Research Assistant/Research Associate (Fixed Term)
description: Applications are invited for a postdoctoral research associate in the lab of Dr Jasper Poort, based at the Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience at the University of Cambridge. The successful candidate will work on a research project that will investigate the neural mechanisms of visual decision-making, learning, and attention. The research combines electrophysiology, and optogenetic manipulation of different cell types and neural projections in visual and decision-making brain areas to understand how mice learn to become experts in different visually-guided decision-making tasks and flexibly switch attention between tasks. The successful applicant will join a supportive and multi-disciplinary research environment including experimental facilities and expertise in the Poort lab ( https://www.pdn.cam.ac.uk/svl/ ) and collaborators. Applicants should have completed (or are about to submit) a PhD (research associate) or (under)graduate degree (research assistant) in neuroscience, biology, or other relevant disciplines. We are looking for someone with previous experience in chronic extracellular electrophysiology (e.g. tetrodes or multichannel probes), behaviour in mice and advanced data analysis skills (e.g. Matlab or Python). Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 2 years in the first instance. Once an offer of employment has been accepted, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a basic disclosure (criminal records check) check and a security check. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click 'Apply' above. To apply for this post, please submit a CV, cover letter, and a 1 page research proposal on 'circuit mechanisms of visually-guided decision-making'. We also need the contact details of two people who can provide a professional reference. The closing date for applications is 8th September 2026. Informal enquiries about the position can be made to Dr Jasper Poort ( jp816@cam.ac.uk ). Please quote reference PM50828 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

title: Researcher in Statistical Epidemiology
description: Location: New Radcliffe House, Radcliffe Observatory, Woodstock Rd, Oxford OX2 6GG The National Perinatal Epidemiology Unit (NPEU) is looking for a Researcher in Statistical Epidemiology to join our research team working on an exciting new programme of research to improve understanding of the longer-term effects of medical interventions in pregnancy on children’s health and development. You will contribute to the design, conduct and analysis of observational studies using large, complex, routinely collected UK health and education data, including CPRD, HES and ECHILD, and methods such as target trial emulation. You will undertake data management and statistical analysis, contribute to the development of study protocols, and draft study reports and papers for peer-reviewed publication. You will work closely with internal and external collaborators, including service users, and contribute to the wider academic activities of the Unit. You will hold an MSc in statistics, epidemiology or a health-related field which includes a substantial amount of biomedical statistics and have substantial experience in health services research and epidemiology. You will have practical experience of managing and analysing large and complex datasets and proficiency in STATA or R. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, experience of preparing documents for publication and drafting manuscripts, and the ability to manage multiple projects and work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team are essential. The post is offered on a full-time basis and is fixed term for three years. Applications for flexible working arrangements are welcomed and will be considered in line with business needs. Applications for part-time working will also be considered, with a minimum commitment of 0.8 FTE. You will be required to upload a CV and supporting statement as part of your online application. Your supporting statement should clearly demonstrate, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet each of the selection criteria for the post. Go to Cover Letters | Oxford University Careers Service for information and advice on writing an effective Supporting Statement. For more information about the role, please contact Dr Kate Fitzpatrick at kate.fitzpatrick@npeu.ox.ac.uk or the recruitment manager at recruitment@wrh.ox.ac.uk . The closing date for applications is 12.00 noon on 21st September 2026. Interviews are expected to take place at the beginning of October. £38,674 to £45,163 per annum. Research Grade 7

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: About the Role We are seeking a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a Pancreatic Cancer UK funded project at the Barts Cancer Institute (BCI), Queen Mary University of London. The project focuses on developing novel urine-based phosphoproteomic biomarkers for the early detection and personalised management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). About You The successful candidate will be completing or will already hold a PhD in relevant field. You will have experience in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and/or phosphoproteomics, including protein extraction, phosphopeptide enrichment, LC-MS/MS workflows, and analysis of proteomics datasets using appropriate bioinformatic and statistical tools. You should have a strong interest in translational cancer research and knowledge of cancer signalling pathways, particularly kinase signalling and phosphorylation biology. Experience working with human biological samples, including urine, plasma or tissue, is essential. Experience with software and analysis tools such as R, Mascot, DIA-NN, or related platforms would be advantageous. About the Institute The Barts Cancer Institute (BCI) is a Cancer Research UK Centre of Excellence whose work aims to transform the lives of those with and at risk of cancer through innovative research in the laboratory, in patients and in populations. It is one of six institutes within The Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry (FMD) BCI is internationally renowned in many areas of cancer research and it combines ground-breaking basic research with the expertise of clinicians and clinician scientists from the Centre for Experimental Cancer Medicine and the Barts NHS Trust to achieve improvements in cancer patient care. BCI is also a partner in the CRUK City of London Major Centre (together with UCL, Kings and the Francis Crick Institute) which is a Centre of Excellence in Biotherapeutics. BCI is committed in supporting and developing future cancer researchers through its extensive postgraduate training. Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

title: Research Associate
description: About the role Are you passionate about engineering biology and developing sustainable solutions to address global environmental challenges? We are seeking an ambitious and highly motivated Post Doctoral Researcher to join the Rodrigo Ledesma-Amaro Lab in the Department of Bioengineering at Imperial College London as part of the PROPEL project, an exciting European collaborative initiative developing next-generation sustainable biomanufacturing technologies. The successful candidate will join the Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein and the Microbial Food Hub, internationally recognised centres driving innovation in engineering biology, precision fermentation and sustainable food systems. Working within a multidisciplinary and collaborative research environment, you will contribute to pioneering research at the interface of synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, microbial biotechnology and bioprocess engineering. This role will focus on engineering the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica to produce high-value lipids using state-of-the-art synthetic biology and metabolic engineering approaches. You will design and construct novel microbial cell factories, optimise metabolic pathways and develop sustainable bioprocesses that contribute to a circular bioeconomy. As part of the PROPEL consortium, you will contribute to developing innovative biological manufacturing platforms that transform renewable and waste-derived carbon sources into valuable bio-based products. The project aims to establish sustainable alternatives to fossil-derived materials by combining advances in synthetic biology, fermentation and waste valorisation, helping accelerate Europe's transition towards greener manufacturing. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research with real-world environmental impact while working alongside leading academic and industrial collaborators across Europe. What you would be doing You will undertake research within the Rodrigo Ledesma-Amaro Laboratory, contributing to the development of sustainable microbial cell factories for lipid production. Your responsibilities will include: Engineering Yarrowia lipolytica using synthetic biology and metabolic engineering approaches. Designing, constructing and characterising engineered yeast strains for lipid biosynthesis. Developing and optimising fermentation and bioprocess strategies. Analysing experimental data and presenting findings at group meetings and scientific conferences. Collaborating with researchers across the PROPEL consortium and contributing to project deliverables, publications and future grant applications. title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: Full time: 35 hours per week Fixed-term: 36 months Vacancies available: 2 The opportunity: This project seeks to realise a new approach to turbulence computation via a combination of modern AI technology (graph neural networks and transformers) with a dynamical systems framework. The dynamical systems viewpoint imagines the turbulence as a space-time tapestry of connected states, which are related to exact solutions of the governing equations in smaller domains. This viewpoint is compelling: it connects dynamical events to statistical properties of the flow, it generates a set of rules by which different recurrent patterns can coexist and interact and it is a robust platform on which to build low-order models for deployment in industrial applications. However, to date this approach has been restricted to small-scale flows because of (1) the computational challenge of identifying the coherent patterns and (2) the combinatorial challenge of identifying the rules by which the patterns join to form the space-time tapestry. These problems are a natural fit for frontier AI models. The two postdocs on this project will, together with the PI, his collaborators and industrial partners, design, train and release these models. These positions are funded by UKRI to work with Dr Jacob Page on the design and construction of large neural networks for the embedding and prediction of high Reynolds number turbulence. The approach is motivated by Hopf’s “dynamical systems” view of turbulent flows. The project includes collaboration with a leading researcher at a major tech company, in addition to ongoing collaborations with Prof Steve Brunton’s group at the University of Washington and Dr Georgios Rigas’ group at Imperial College London. There will also be scope for involvement in other ongoing industrial collaborations. £41,064 to £48,822 per annum (Grade 7)

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: Full time: 35 hours per week Fixed term: 2 years Vacancies: 2 The role is part of AI²: Assurance and Insurance for Artificial Intelligence, a major research programme on insuring AI systems. The project is a collaboration between the University of Edinburgh, the University of Oxford, the University of Warwick and AXA. It aims to develop the mathematical, statistical and computational foundations needed to evaluate, price, monitor and mitigate risks arising from AI systems, including generative and agentic AI. description: Location: South Kensington Campus About the role: We are looking for motivated individuals to Join the Formal Methods in AI (FMAI) lab at Imperial College London, led by Dr. Francesco Belardinelli , in a fully funded postdoctoral research role to lead transformative research in formal methods for safe reinforcement learning. Overview . The FMAI lab at Imperial is seeking highly motivated & talented Postdoctoral Research Associates (PDRAs/PostDocs), who have demonstrated competence in conducting cutting-edge research. The position is fully funded in the context of Dr. Francesco Belardinelli’s ARIA project Enforcing Safety in Cyber-Physical Systems via Proof Certificates , and focus on the design, development, and application of Safe RL algorithms as well as their verification via Proof Certificates , including monitoring & shielding of cyber-physical systems. AI-powered cyber-physical systems must operate continuously and reactively in safety-critical environments. Failures pose severe economic risks, even cost human lives. In recent years, Safe RL has been developed to apply RL techniques in safety-critical environments. However, current methods primarily provide finite-horizon, statistical, or asymptotic guaranties, and fail to ensure strict safety compliance at runtime. This creates a fundamental gap between scalable learning & certifiable safety. To address this gap, this project aims at developing Certified Reinforcement Learning , a neuro-symbolic framework for learning safe controllers in real-world cyber-physical systems that leverages the scalability and adaptability of RL, while providing the formal, verifiable guaranties associated with Formal Methods. The proposed methodology will be implemented in the MASA-Safe-RL library – an open-source platform for Safe RL currently being developed at the FMAI lab. What you would be doing: Within the project, you will conduct original research in the new & exciting field of Formal Methods for Safe RL and explore its applications across cyber-physical systems. You will work closely with Dr Hongye Zhang and EU/UK academic/industrial partners across the project consortium, contributing to project milestones, technical reports, publications and presentations. We are looking for a highly motivated researcher with a PhD, or equivalent experience, in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, thermal engineering, aerospace engineering, physics or a related discipline. You should have strong analytical and research skills, together with knowledge or experience relevant to electric machines, applied superconductivity, or aerospace technologies. Experience with electro-mechanical-thermal modelling, cryogenic systems, superconducting materials, motor windings or hydrogen-electric propulsion would be advantageous. The role offers an opportunity to contribute to internationally significant research addressing the transition to cleaner aviation. Occasional travel to consortium meetings, conferences or partner facilities may be required. Laboratory work may involve cryogenic liquids, including liquid nitrogen, and will be supported by appropriate training and risk assessments. We encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences who can contribute to our values of excellence, integrity, inclusion, relevance and ambition. Apply now to join the project team and help develop innovative propulsion technologies for the future of sustainable aviation. A career with us has a range of other benefits that can be tailored to your lifestyle, including: A competitive pension scheme Generous annual leave allowance Staff discounts and a wide range of health and wellbeing support Professional development and training opportunities Family-friendly and inclusive policies Employee networks and support for a diverse and welcoming community £41,064 to £48,822 per annum (Grade 7)

title: Clinical Research Fellow (PhD) in Biliary Tract Cancer Liquid Biopsy Translational Research
description: Salary: £65,048 - £73,992 per annum (according to relevant experience) aligned to NHS Resident Doctors Pay Scale Post Start Date: January 2027 About The Fellowship Applicants will undertake a 3-year fully funded PhD fellowship (The University of Manchester) in cancer research through the highly successful CRUK PhD programme, supervised by internationally recognised scientists and clinical academics. The fellowship will be predominantly laboratory-based with opportunities to gain experience in novel liquid biopsy technologies and training in bioinformatics and computational analysis whilst maintaining clinical engagement within the Hepato-pancreatico-biliary (HPB) Medical Oncology Team at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust. This PhD will investigate the development and clinical application of circulating nucleic acid biomarkers to improve the diagnosis, prognostication and treatment stratification of patients with biliary tract cancers (BTC). Despite advances in systemic therapies, BTC remains associated with poor survival and there is an urgent need for minimally invasive biomarkers that enable earlier diagnosis, molecular characterisation and real-time monitoring of treatment response. The successful candidate will undertake translational laboratory research within the Nucleic Acid Biomarker Team at the CRUK National Biomarker Centre, working alongside leading scientists, bioinformaticians and clinician researchers. Supervised by Dr A Conway (Senior Clinical Lecturer and Honorary Consultant in Medical Oncology) and Dr A Clipson (Deputy Team Lead Nucleic Acid Biomarker Team), the project will focus on the development and validation of novel liquid biopsy approaches including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), cell-free RNA (cfRNA) and other circulating biomarkers from blood and bile samples. The fellow will gain extensive training in molecular biology techniques, next-generation sequencing technologies, biomarker assay development, experimental design, statistical analysis and bioinformatics. They will also have opportunities to collaborate with national and international research partners and present their work at major scientific conferences. About You We are seeking a talented and enthusiastic clinical academic, passionate about cancer research, who has a strong academic track record and a clear commitment to pursuing a career in clinical academia. The successful applicant will be intellectually curious, self-motivated and capable of working both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research environment. You will have a Medical Degree (MB, ChB or equivalent), full General Medical Council (GMC) registration with licence to practise in the UK and MRCP, FRCP (or equivalent qualifications) along with relevant clinical or medical oncology experience. You will have previous laboratory-based research experience. Previous experience of management of patients in clinical trials would be an advantage. You will possess excellent communication and organisational skills, with the ability to critically evaluate scientific literature, manage competing priorities and contribute effectively to collaborative research projects. Prior laboratory research experience is desirable but not essential, as comprehensive training and mentorship will be provided throughout the fellowship. This fellowship is ideally suited to clinicians who aspire to become future leaders in translational cancer research and who are motivated to improve outcomes for patients with biliary tract cancer through innovative biomarker discovery and precision medicine. Apply Now Please submit your online application by 18:00 on 07 September 2026 Monday For any informal enquiries about this post, please contact Alicia-Marie Conway, alicia-marie.conway@cruk.manchester.ac.uk or Alexandra Clipson alexandra.clipson@cruk.manchester.ac.uk

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Topological Machine Learning and Generative AI
description: Location: Dublin Innovation Institute, Block 6 Founders District, Belfield Office Park, Beech Hill Road, Dublin 4, Ireland Working arrangement: Full Time on site at the Dublin Innovation Institute Click to read more about the Dublin Innovation Institute (DII) : https://dublininstitute.northeastern.edu/about/ Term: 10 months, full time Reports to: Dr. Shashi Murthy, Head of Institute. Prof. Giovanni Petri Start: 1 September 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter The role Northeastern University's Dublin Innovation Institute (DII) wishes to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate to work on TOPO-LLM: Topologically-Informed Large Language Models for Innovation Intelligence . The project is funded by FFplus, a EuroHPC Joint Undertaking initiative under the European Union's Digital Europe Programme, and brings together DII and Futurity Systems, a Barcelona-based technology company developing AI tools for innovation and competitive intelligence. TOPO-LLM asks whether large language models can reason more effectively about scientific and technological innovation when they are given explicit information about the higher-order structure of the underlying data. The project will combine topological data analysis, higher-order network methods and large-scale language-model training on a knowledge graph of scientific publications, patents and related innovation data. The appointed researcher will lead DII's scientific contribution. The main task is to design and validate an Innovation Topology Embedding: a compact representation built from persistent-homology summaries, higher-order Laplacian features and multiscale network structure. The researcher will develop scalable methods for computing these features on a very large knowledge graph, integrate them into a transformer-based language model, and test their value through carefully controlled benchmarks and ablation studies. This is a deliberately interdisciplinary role. We are looking for someone who combines a strong foundation in topological or geometric methods with the ability to implement and evaluate machine-learning systems at scale. Candidates may come from topological data analysis, geometric deep learning, network science, statistical physics, machine learning, or a closely related field. We recognise that few applicants will be equally strong in every area; where a candidate's experience is weighted towards either topology or machine-learning engineering, we particularly value evidence that they can collaborate across the boundary and learn quickly. The researcher will be based at DII on the University College Dublin campus and will join Prof. Giovanni Petri's research group, NP Lab , within Northeastern's Network Science Institute London. They will work closely with the Futurity Systems team in Barcelona and with collaborators across Northeastern's global network. The project includes access to the EuroHPC MareNostrum 5 supercomputer at the Barcelona Supercomputing Centre. We provide an opportunity to carry out academically substantive research in close contact with an industry partner. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to research publications, project reports and reusable research software arising from the work, subject to the project's collaboration and intellectual-property agreements. We know diversity fosters creativity and innovation. We are committed to equality of opportunity, to being fair and inclusive, and to being a place where all belong. We therefore particularly encourage applications from candidates who are likely to be underrepresented in the applicant pool. Dublin Innovation Institute and the research group Northeastern University's Dublin Innovation Institute serves as a bridge between the University's global network and the European research ecosystem. Located on the campus of University College Dublin, DII offers opportunities for collaboration across Europe and North America. Its current projects span political science, computer science and network science, and this appointment will form part of the Institute's initial cohort of research staff. The position will be part of NPLab, led by Prof. Giovanni Petri, Professor of Network Science at Northeastern University London and core faculty at the Network Science Institute. The group works at the intersection of higher-order network science, topological data analysis and information theory, with applications in machine learning, neuroscience, collective behaviour and animal communication. NPLab brings together doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in London and across Northeastern's global network. This post is funded by FFplus. The research directly relevant to the position sits within the group's wider work on higher-order Laplacian renormalisation, higher-order connectomics, and topological representations of complex systems. Prof. Petri leads a broader research programme in this area, including as Principal Investigator on the ERC Consolidator Grant RUNES and Project CETI, and as Co-Investigator on the BeyondTheEdge Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network, giving the group a rich international research environment beyond this specific project. Network Science Institute Northeastern University's Network Science Institute (NetSI) brings together researchers from the physical, information, biological and social sciences to develop the theory and applications of complex networks. Founded in Boston in 2014, NetSI now connects research communities across Northeastern's global network, including its London hub. The successful candidate will join this international and highly interdisciplinary community. About Northeastern University Founded in 1898, Northeastern is a global research university and a recognised leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. Its locations across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland create opportunities for collaborative, solutions-focused research across disciplines and regions. Northeastern University is an equal opportunity employer, seeking to recruit and support a broadly diverse community of faculty and staff. Northeastern values and celebrates diversity in all its forms and strives to foster an inclusive culture built on respect. Job Duties The appointed researcher will carry out independent research, analyse and publish results, prepare project reports and technical documentation, and contribute to the wider research environment at DII and NPLab. Job duties will include the following, with the distribution of time varying across the project: 60-70% Research and implementation: design the Innovation Topology Embedding; develop and scale the topology-computation pipeline; integrate topological features into the language model; and run controlled evaluations and ablation studies. 15-20% Research communication: prepare publications, project deliverables, presentations and documentation for research software. 10-15% Project collaboration: coordinate technical work with Futurity Systems, manage use of the EuroHPC allocation, and report progress against project milestones. 5-10% Research-group activity: participate in NP Lab and Network Science Institute meetings and contribute to the group's collaborative research culture. Person Specification Criteria A PhD, awarded or near completion by the start date, in computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, network science, or a related quantitative discipline. Research experience in at least one of the following: topological data analysis; computational topology; geometric or topological deep learning; higher-order network science; graph machine learning; or statistical physics of complex systems. Strong programming skills in Python and experience with modern scientific or machine-learning software. Experience designing, running and interpreting computational experiments. Demonstrated ability to plan, execute and publish independent research. Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly in written and spoken English. A collaborative working style, strong personal initiative and the ability to deliver against project milestones. We recognise that excellent candidates may not match every item listed above. If your background is adjacent and you are excited by the project, we encourage you to apply. Additional desired skills and experience: Practical experience with persistent homology or related topological descriptors, using tools such as GUDHI, Ripser, giotto-tda, or equivalent. Experience with transformers or large language models, including fine-tuning, continued pretraining, representation learning, or model evaluation. Experience with PyTorch and the Hugging Face ecosystem. Experience with high-performance computing, SLURM, distributed multi-GPU training, or large-scale checkpointing. Familiarity with hypergraphs, simplicial complexes, higher-order Laplacians, network renormalization, or multiscale graph methods. Experience with large knowledge graphs, sparse linear algebra, graph databases, or bibliometric and patent data. A track record in open-source scientific software or research collaborations with external partners. Additional Information Enquiries Informal enquiries may be made to Prof. Giovanni Petri at giovanni.petri@nulondon.ac.uk and are warmly encouraged. To be considered for the position, applications must be made in accordance with the process specified in the final advertisement. Application Process The panel will be shortlisting for this position on a rolling basis so please apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close this post before the closing date if we receive a large number of applications. Applications should be made to Caroline Ward, HR Director (caroline.ward@nulondon.ac.uk) by 12pm on Wednesday 09 September 2026 . Please reference TOPO-LLM-DII-2026 in your application. Please ensure that your application includes the following: A CV, including a publication list and details of relevant software or open-source contributions. A covering letter explaining how you meet the selection criteria and why you are interested in the role. A research statement of no more than two pages and at least 1 figure, describing your relevant work and how you would approach the first six months of the project. Names and contact information for up to three referees. References will only be sought for shortlisted candidates. Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed by video call. The interview will include a technical discussion of the candidate's relevant work and of the practical challenges involved in scaling topological methods and language-model training. Eligibility to work. Due to DII’s current staffing requirements, at this time we are only able to appoint an EEA, UK or Swiss national to this role. Applicants must also be able to demonstrate their entitlement to work in Ireland. Please describe your status in your covering letter. €64,000 for 10 month project period

title: Research Associate
description: About the role: This is a rare opportunity for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher, with a strong background in quantitative methods and work, welfare and health research, to shape the evidence base on youth trajectories into economic inactivity, benefit receipt and work, as part of a major programme funded by the Colt Foundation at King’s College London. You will work across some of the UK’s richest linked datasets including Department for Work and Pensions and HMRC administrative data via the new RAPID linkage, the Longitudinal Educational Outcomes (LEO) dataset, and major birth cohorts such as Next Steps via the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration (UK LLC). You will apply advanced statistical methods including time to event and competing risk models, sequence analysis and multilevel modelling, and will lead a systematic review as part of this work to address research questions that are policy relevant. You will work closely with the Principal Investigators of this programme of work, Professor Sharon Stevelink and Professor Ioannis Bakolis, as well as the work package leads, colleagues across the Department of Psychological Medicine, Health Services and Population Research Department, King’s Policy Institute and King’s Business School, and our lived experience partners, whose voices you will help embed throughout the research. You will also line manage/supervise a Research Assistant. Experience across a range of health and administrative data sources (e.g. RAPID, LEO, UK birth cohorts) and linked data sources would be an advantage, as well as past experience of engaging with a wide range of stakeholders and having contributed to outputs beyond scientific publications such as policy briefings, infographics or government consultation responses. You will be supported to developing your academic career, including a research visit to our international collaborators in Norway, access to a range of training courses, and dedicated support with fellowship and grant applications. This is a full time (35 hours per week), based at King’s College London (Denmark Hill campus) for 4 days a week with the option to work from home for 1 day a week. You will be offered an a fixed term contract until 18 th October 2029 Research staff at King’s are entitled to at least 10 days per year (pro-rata) for professional development. This entitlement, from the Concordat to Support the Career Development of Researchers , applies to Postdocs, Research Assistants, Research and Teaching Technicians, Teaching Fellows and AEP equivalent up to and including grade 7. Visit the Centre for Research Staff Development for more information. £45,031 to £48,607 per annum, including London Weighting Allowance

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: About the Role A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is available in Dr Alex de Mendoza’s laboratory in the Department of Biology, School of Biological and Behavioural Sciences, Queen Mary University of London. Building on ongoing work in the group on the evolution of adenine DNA methylation in eukaryotic genomes ( www.demendozalab.com ), this project will investigate the regulatory roles of this epigenetic mark using synthetic biology approaches. In particular, it will leverage heterologous expression systems to test the role of 6mA methyltransferases, aiming to understand their deposition patterns and effects on the wide epigenome. The project will leverage laboratory experience in heterologous and evolutionary inspired synthetic epigenomics to decode an ancestral regulatory pathway so far poorly understood. The post is full-time, with an initial contract of 1.5 years, with the possibility of extension subject to funding. The main responsibilities include performing synthetic biology, comparative genomics, epigenome engineering and preparation of manuscripts for publication. There will also be opportunities to contribute to supervision of students and to collaborate with international partners. About You The ideal candidate will have a PhD or be about to defend one in Genetics, Evolution, Biochemistry, or a related field. Have experience with epigenetics and cell culture / molecular biology. With desirable skills include experience in omics data analysis and working on mammalian cell cultures. You will hold strong communication skills and effective collaboration, with demonstrable outcomes. Self-motivation, teamwork abilities, and excellent research management skills. Informal enquiries please contact Dr Alex de Mendoza ( a.demendoza@qmul.ac.uk ). About the School/Department/Institute/Project The role sits within the School of Biological and Behavioural Sciences, one of the largest Schools within Queen Mary University of London. The school has a strong research output and demanding educational standards for its students, but all members benefit from a high level of academic and social integration. In addition, the school is committed to equality of opportunity and holds a Silver Athena SWAN Award. About Queen Mary At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable. Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers. We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form. Benefits We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities. Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly. £38,419 to £44,288 per annum

title: M-RIC Research Assistant - Clinical Trials Support
description: We are looking to appoint a Research Assistant to work for the Mental Health Research for innovation Centre (M-RIC) which is part of the university Centre; Civic Health Innovation Labs (CHIL). M-RIC is an ambitious programme of work jointly delivered between University of Liverpool and Mersey care NHS Foundation Trust (MCFT). It has wide reaching benefits to the region whilst raising the profile of all partners as leaders in Mental Health Innovation. The ideal candidate will: Support the delivery of research studies, clinical trials and innovation projects across M-RIC work packages. Support project teams to deliver studies in line with agreed milestones, timelines and regulatory requirements Contribute to study reporting, monitoring and governance activities, providing updates to project leads and relevant committees as required. Working collaboratively with NHS and wider partners on M-RIC aligned projects Engage closely with PPIE colleagues in M-RIC and other infrastructure grants to progress and develop best practice principles Engage in relevant training and academic advancement relevant to the postholder’s interests and career ambitions Support the development of funding applications, study documentation and research dissemination activities as appropriate. For full details and to apply online, please visit: recruit.liverpool.ac.uk £33,951 to £38,784 per annum (Grade 6)
